title: Mutually refining section opens give isomorphic Proj neighborhoods
statement: Let $B$ be an affine scheme and let $q:Y\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $Y$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated, meaning that intersections of affine opens of $Y$ are quasi-compact. Let $L,K$ be invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with section rings $A_L=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes n})$ and $A_K=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\Gamma(Y,K^{\otimes n})$ [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. For a positive-degree section $s$ of either module write $Y_s$ for its nonvanishing open [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Assume that both families of these opens cover $Y$. Assume further the following two refinement conditions: for every $n>0$, $t\in\Gamma(Y,K^{\otimes n})$ and $y\in Y_t$, there exist $d>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes d})$ with $y\in Y_s\subseteq Y_t$; and for every $d>0$, $s\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes d})$ and $y\in Y_s$, there exist $n>0$ and $t\in\Gamma(Y,K^{\otimes n})$ with $y\in Y_t\subseteq Y_s$. Put $P_L=\operatorname{Proj}(A_L)$ and $P_K=\operatorname{Proj}(A_K)$ [def-pc-proj], with $B$-structure induced by $q$, and let $r_L:Y\to P_L$ and $r_K:Y\to P_K$ be the canonical maps [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map]. There are open subschemes $V_L\subseteq P_L$, $V_K\subseteq P_K$ [def-weil-open-immersion] containing respectively $r_L(Y)$ and $r_K(Y)$, and a $B$-isomorphism $\theta:V_L\xrightarrow{\sim}V_K$ such that $\theta\circ r_L=r_K$ after factoring the two maps through these opens.

source.place: Agent-formulated comparison lemma from Tag 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), used to supply the omitted comparison in Guo Proposition 6.2. The comparison is not stated verbatim by this tag; its affine chart gluing argument is written in report.md.

proof.text: For $M=L,K$ write $D_M(s)=D_+(s)\subset P_M$. By lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map, $r_M^{-1}D_M(s)=Y_s$ and the ring map $\rho_{M,s}:\Gamma(D_M(s),\mathcal O)= (A_M)_{(s)}\to\Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal O_Y)$ sends $\xi/s^a$ to $\xi|_{Y_s}/s^a$. Apply lem-sc-section-ring-localization-bijective: $Y$ is qcqs and $s$ has positive degree, and its required identity follows by multiplying this fraction formula by $s^a$. Thus every $\rho_{M,s}$ is a ring isomorphism, without assuming $Y_s$ affine.

source.place: Tags 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), clause (1) and chart formula; 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), qcqs isomorphism

proof.text: The standard opens $D_M(s)$ form a basis of $P_M$: the complement of a homogeneous vanishing set is a union of these opens, and $D_M(s)\cap D_M(s\prime)=D_M(ss\prime)$ by the prime-ideal description in def-pc-proj. The canonical sheaf morphism $\mathcal O_{P_M}\to(r_M)_*\mathcal O_Y$ evaluates on this basis to the isomorphisms of Step 1. Apply clause (b) of lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis with values in commutative rings. It is therefore an isomorphism on all opens. In particular, for every open $W\subset P_M$, the restriction $r_M^{-1}(W)\to W$ is scheme-theoretically dominant, meaning that the induced map $\mathcal O_W\to(r_M|_{r_M^{-1}(W)})_*\mathcal O_{r_M^{-1}(W)}$ is injective.

source.place: Tags 009O (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence) and 009R (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-structures); Proj basis from constructions.tex, standard opens

proof.text: For every pair $(s,t)$ of positive-degree sections with $Y_s\subseteq Y_t$, define a ring map $\Gamma(D_K(t),\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(D_L(s),\mathcal O)$ as $\rho_{L,s}^{-1}\circ\operatorname{res}_{Y_t,Y_s}\circ\rho_{K,t}$. The affine-target correspondence lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme gives a morphism $h_{s,t}:D_L(s)\to D_K(t)$. Its composite with $r_L|_{Y_s}$ equals $r_K|_{Y_s}$ as maps into $D_K(t)$: both induce the ring map $\operatorname{res}_{Y_t,Y_s}\circ\rho_{K,t}$, since $\rho_{L,s}\rho_{L,s}^{-1}$ is the identity. It is a $B$-morphism, since the two maps from $D_L(s)$ to the affine $B$ induce the same ring map from $\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$ after the injective map $\rho_{L,s}$; both then become $q|_{Y_s}$.

source.place: Tags 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) and 01HY (lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes); agent construction of the comparison ring map

proof.text: Let $U_L$ be the union of all $D_L(s)$ occurring in pairs of Step 3. For $y\in Y$ choose a $K$-section $t$ nonvanishing at $y$ using its cover, and then an $L$-section $s$ with $y\in Y_s\subseteq Y_t$ using the first refinement hypothesis. Hence $r_L(Y)\subset U_L$. On an overlap $W=D_L(s)\cap D_L(s\prime)$, the two constructed maps to $P_K$ agree after $r_L^{-1}W\to W$, since both composites are $r_K$ there. Step 2 supplies scheme-theoretic dominance of this test map. The target $P_K$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by lem-trf-proj-separated. Apply lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ (all scheme maps have the same composite to this terminal scheme). Thus the maps agree on overlaps, including two choices of $t$ for the same $s$. The gluing lemma gives a $B$-morphism $h:U_L\to P_K$ with $h r_L=r_K$.

source.place: Tag 01KM (lemma-where-are-they-equal), closed equalizer; Tag 01JA (gluing); constructions.tex Tag 01MC (lemma-proj-separated)

proof.text: Perform Steps 3--4 with $L,K$ interchanged, using pairs $(t,s)$ with $Y_t\subseteq Y_s$. The ring map is now $\rho_{K,t}^{-1}\circ\operatorname{res}_{Y_s,Y_t}\circ\rho_{L,s}$. The $L$-section cover and the second refinement hypothesis ensure that the union $U_K$ of these $D_K(t)$ contains $r_K(Y)$. On overlaps the composites agree after the restrictions of $r_K$, which are scheme-theoretically dominant by Step 2, and the separated target is now $P_L$. The same affine correspondence, separated-target uniqueness and gluing statements give a $B$-morphism $k:U_K\to P_L$ with $k r_K=r_L$.

source.place: Tags 01I1, 01KM and 01JA; constructions.tex Tag 01MC; symmetric chart construction

proof.text: Put $V_L=U_L\cap h^{-1}(U_K)$ and $V_K=U_K\cap k^{-1}(U_L)$. These are open and contain the respective images, because $h r_L=r_K$ and $k r_K=r_L$. On $V_L$, compare $k h:V_L\to P_L$ with its inclusion into $P_L$. Their composites with $Y=r_L^{-1}(V_L)\to V_L$ are both $r_L$. By Step 2 this test map is scheme-theoretically dominant, and $P_L$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The separated-target uniqueness lemma gives $k h=\operatorname{id}$ on $V_L$, as maps to $P_L$. Interchanging $L,K$ gives $h k=\operatorname{id}$ on $V_K$, as maps to $P_K$.

source.place: Tag 01KM (lemma-where-are-they-equal), applied to the two compositions; constructions.tex Tag 01MC

proof.text: For $x\in V_L$, $h(x)\in U_K$ and $k(h(x))=x\in U_L$, so $h(x)\in V_K$. Likewise $k(V_K)\subseteq V_L$. Thus $h$ and $k$ restrict to morphisms $V_L\to V_K$ and $V_K\to V_L$. The equalities of Step 6 show that these restrictions are inverse (an open-subscheme morphism is its ambient morphism with codomain restricted). They are $B$-morphisms by their construction. Set $\theta=h|_{V_L}$. Its composite with $r_L$ is $r_K$, as established before restriction, proving all clauses.

source.place: Open subschemes: Tag 01IO; agent restriction of the constructed inverse morphisms
